questions.q: Why does kernel launch overhead matter for a training step made of many small kernels?
options: Each kernel launch requires reloading the CUDA driver from disk
Dispatching each kernel has a fixed CPU-side cost regardless of the kernel's actual runtime, and that cost adds up across hundreds of small launches
Small kernels always run out of registers
Launch overhead only affects memory-bound kernels
questions.explain: The CPU has to prepare and dispatch every kernel launch, and that fixed per-launch cost becomes a significant fraction of step time when there are many small kernels.

questions.q: What does a CUDA Graph capture?
options: A screenshot of GPU memory usage over time
An entire sequence of kernel launches, memory operations, and their dependencies, recorded as a single replayable structure
The source code of all kernels in a Python file
A log of past nvidia-smi readings
questions.explain: A CUDA Graph records a full sequence of operations and their dependencies, which can then be launched as one unit instead of many separate CPU dispatches.

questions.q: After capturing a graph, why does the training loop call `static_input.copy_(data)` instead of reassigning `static_input = data`?
options: Reassignment is faster but less readable
A captured graph replays the same kernels against the same fixed memory addresses, so new data must be copied into the existing static tensor rather than pointed to a new one
copy_() automatically moves data to pinned memory
Reassignment would delete the CUDA graph entirely
questions.explain: CUDA Graph replay depends on the captured operations referencing the same memory addresses every time, so updating data in place via copy_() is required.

questions.q: What kind of operation cannot be captured as-is in a CUDA Graph?
options: A fixed sequence of matrix multiplications
An operation whose control flow or shape depends on the actual data, like a dynamic sequence length or a data-dependent branch
A convolution layer
An optimizer step
questions.explain: Because a graph replays the exact same recorded operations every time, any control flow that must be re-decided based on the data each time can't be captured directly.

questions.q: In which scenario does CUDA Graph capture-and-replay offer the least benefit?
options: A model with hundreds of small elementwise and normalization kernels
A tight, fixed-shape inference loop
A model dominated by a few large kernels, where launch overhead was never a significant fraction of step time
A model already optimized with mixed precision, making launch overhead relatively larger
questions.explain: CUDA Graphs amortize per-launch overhead. If a model's time is dominated by a few large kernels rather than many small launches, that overhead was never the bottleneck, so there's little to gain.
